summary: Taylor Morrison's article argues that diet is a powerful form of preventive medicine, tracing the idea from ancient Greek, Chinese and Ayurvedic traditions to modern research on antioxidants, fiber, whole foods and dietary patterns. It cites several experts and events on whole foods, superfoods, the Mediterranean and Japanese diets, and personalized nutrition. It also notes challenges such as food deserts and the need to consult healthcare professionals before major dietary changes.
one_line: Taylor Morrison's article explores food as preventive medicine, linking ancient traditions with modern nutrition science, dietary patterns, personalized plans, and access challenges.
key_facts: The article by Taylor Morrison is dated September 15, 2023 and covers nutritional therapies and food as medicine.
Hippocrates asserted, "Let food be thy medicine and medicine be thy food."
Ancient Chinese practice classified food and herbs by energies and healing properties to balance yin and yang; Ayurveda uses dietary adjustments aligned with one's dosha.

Dr. Anne Parker, a nutritionist, spoke at the International Conference on Nutrition and Medicine on October 4, 2023, about antioxidants in fruits and vegetables reducing cellular damage and chronic disease risk such as cancer and heart disease.

Research led by Dr. Conrad Roberts in the "Journal of Nutritional Science" on November 10, 2023 showed fibers from whole grains and legumes aid gut health and help prevent irritable bowel syndrome and Crohn's disease.

Registered dietitian Melissa Thompson gave a seminar on September 29, 2023 explaining that whole foods contain vitamins, minerals, phytochemicals and antioxidants that work synergistically, unlike isolated supplements.
Dietitian Emma Johnson led a workshop on September 20, 2023 advocating a variety of superfoods such as blueberries, kale and salmon, valued for antioxidants, vitamins and omega-3 fatty acids.
Cardiologist Michael Davidson said at a healthcare summit on September 25, 2023 that the Mediterranean diet can significantly improve heart health.
Dietitian Sophia Lee discussed on October 15, 2023 how the traditional Japanese diet may contribute to Japan's low obesity rates and long life expectancy.

Clinical nutritionist Elizabeth Gonzalez showcased a pilot program at the National Wellness Conference on September 22, 2023 creating individualized nutrition plans to prevent diabetes using family history, lifestyle and health status.
Food deserts, where healthy food is scarce or expensive, are a significant barrier to using food as medicine.
People, especially those with pre-existing conditions or on medication, should consult healthcare professionals before significant dietary changes to avoid adverse interactions.
